title: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design - Arts - Categories
exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
subject: Arts

questions.q: Which of the following art practices falls under Applied Art?
questions.explain: Textile design is a form of Applied Art because it combines artistic design with a functional everyday object (fabric/clothing). Painting and sculpture (options a and b) are fine arts.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Fine Arts are sub-divided into two main parts. What are they?
questions.explain: Fine Arts are often broadly subdivided into 2D arts (like drawing, painting) and 3D arts (like sculpture, architecture).
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: A professional who creates artwork primarily to decorate and beautify spaces (like living rooms or offices) focuses on which sub-discipline of art?
questions.explain: Aesthetics, beautification, and interior decoration deal specifically with making a living environment or space visually appealing and harmonious.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Adire (tie-dye) and Batik are traditional Nigerian examples of which category of art?
questions.explain: Adire and Batik are traditional methods of resist-dyeing fabric to create patterns. They are classic examples of Textile Design.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which piece of equipment is essential in the production of woven textiles (like Aso-Oke)?
questions.explain: A loom is a device used to weave cloth and tapestry by interlacing warp and weft threads. The potter's wheel and kiln are for ceramics, and the palette is for painting.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Ceramics can best be described as the art of making functional or decorative objects out of what primary material?
questions.explain: Ceramics is the art and science of making objects from inorganic, non-metallic materials, primarily clay, and hardening them by heating them in a kiln.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: In ceramic art, the process of baking molded clay in a high-temperature oven to make it hard and durable is called:
questions.explain: Firing is the process of baking clay objects in a kiln at high temperatures. It permanently changes the chemical structure of the clay, making it rock-hard. Glazing is adding a glassy coating.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which category of Applied Art involves creating posters, book covers, product packages, and digital layouts?
questions.explain: Graphic design is the art of visual communication that combines images, words, and ideas to convey information to an audience, commonly through posters, logos, and packaging.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Typography, the art of arranging text or letters, is primarily a skill required in which field of art?
questions.explain: Typography is heavily utilized in Graphic Design. It is the technique of arranging type (letters/fonts) to make written language legible, readable, and visually appealing.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Aesthetic design is principally concerned with what aspect of an object or environment?
options: Its beauty, visual appeal, and taste
questions.explain: Aesthetics is a core principle in art and design that focuses on the study of beauty, visual appeal, and taste.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: A three-dimensional artwork that has length, breadth, and height, and can often be viewed from all sides is called:
questions.explain: Sculpture is a 3-dimensional art form. When it can be seen from all angles, it is called a sculpture 'in-the-round'. When figures are attached to a flat background, it is a 'relief' sculpture.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a common material used in traditional Sculpture?
questions.explain: Watercolor pigment is a medium used in painting (a two-dimensional art form). Wood, bronze, and stone are standard materials for creating three-dimensional sculptures.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Carving and Modeling are techniques primarily associated with which type of art?
questions.explain: Carving (a subtractive process, like cutting away wood or stone) and modeling (an additive process, like shaping clay) are the foundational techniques of Sculpture.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: The art form that involves applying pigment (colour) suspended in a medium (like oil or water) to a flat surface such as a canvas or paper is called:
questions.explain: Painting is defined by the application of pigments (often liquid) to a two-dimensional surface, creating a visual image or design.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: In painting, an artist frequently uses a flat surface with a thumb hole to hold and mix their colors. What is this tool called?
questions.explain: A palette is a rigid, flat surface on which a painter arranges and mixes paints. An easel is the stand that holds the canvas, and a loom and kiln belong to textile and ceramic arts, respectively.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts
